title: Can, Passive, Causative & Transitivity
description: Potential forms and ことができる, the passive (られる), causative (させる), causative-passive (させられる), and transitive/intransitive verb pairs.

points.title: られる (1) / potential: can, be able to
points.summary: Godan: u → e + る (読める). Ichidan: る → られる (食べられる). する → できる, 来る → 来られる. The object usually takes が.
points.body:
**Formation:**
- **Godan**: final u → **e + る**: 読む → 読**める**, 書く → 書**ける**, 話す → 話**せる**, 買う → 買**える**
- **Ichidan**: drop る + **られる**: 食べる → 食べ**られる**, 見る → 見**られる**
- **する** → **できる**; **来る** → **来られる (こられる)**

The result is an ichidan verb: 読めます, 読めない, 読めた.

**Particle:** the object usually switches from を to **が**: 漢字**が**読めます, 日本語**が**話せます. (を is also heard, especially with longer phrases.)

**ら抜き言葉:** in casual speech, 食べ**れる** and 来**れる** (dropping ら) are very common, but they're considered non-standard. Use 食べ**られる** in tests and formal writing.

The ichidan potential looks identical to the passive (食べられる); context decides.
examples: {漢字|かんじ}が{読|よ}めますか。
Can you read kanji?
{納豆|なっとう}は{食|た}べられません。
I can't eat natto.
{来週|らいしゅう}のパーティーに{来|こ}られますか。
Can you come to next week's party?

points.title: ことができる: can, be able to (formal)
points.summary: Dictionary form + ことができる = 'can do'. It's more formal and written than the potential form. Nouns: 日本語ができる.
points.body:
**Dictionary form + こと + が + できる** expresses ability or possibility:
- ピアノを弾く**ことができます** (I can play the piano).
- ここでたばこを吸う**ことはできません** (smoking isn't possible / allowed here).

**Noun + ができる:** 日本語**が**できます, テニス**が**できる. Here the noun takes **が**.

**ことができる vs potential form:** same meaning, but ことができる is **more formal**. It's common in writing, signs and announcements, and it also expresses circumstantial possibility (rules, permissions). The potential form (弾ける) is more natural in conversation.

Don't use の here (弾くのができる ✗). It must be こと.
examples: {姉|あね}はピアノを{弾|ひ}くことができます。
My older sister can play the piano.
この{図書館|としょかん}では、{本|ほん}を{三冊|さんさつ}まで{借|か}りることができます。
At this library you can borrow up to three books.
{日本語|にほんご}ができますか。
Can you speak Japanese?

points.title: られる (2) / passive: be done (to)
points.summary: Godan: u → a + れる (読まれる). Ichidan: る → られる. する → される, 来る → 来られる. The doer is marked with に. Japanese also has a 'suffering' passive.
points.body:
**Formation:**
- **Godan**: final u → **a + れる**: 読む → 読**まれる**, 書く → 書**かれる**, 言う → 言**われる** (う → **わ**)
- **Ichidan**: drop る + **られる**: 褒める → 褒め**られる**
- **する** → **される**; **来る** → **来られる (こられる)**

**Structure:** [person affected]は + [doer]**に** + passive verb: わたしは先生**に**褒め**られました**.

**Three uses:**
- **Direct passive**: 先生に褒められた (I was praised by the teacher).
- **Suffering passive** (something unpleasant happens *to* you, even with intransitive verbs): 雨に降**られた** (I got rained on), 弟にケーキを食べ**られた** (my brother ate my cake, to my annoyance).
- **Neutral/impersonal** (things, facts): この歌は世界中で歌わ**れています**.

The ichidan passive looks the same as the potential (食べられる).
examples: {先生|せんせい}に{褒|ほ}められました。
I was praised by my teacher.
{雨|あめ}に{降|ふ}られて、びしょびしょになりました。
I got caught in the rain and was soaked.
この{歌|うた}は{世界中|せかいじゅう}で{歌|うた}われています。
This song is sung all over the world.

points.title: させる: make / let someone do
points.summary: Godan: u → a + せる (読ませる). Ichidan: る → させる. する → させる, 来る → 来させる. The person made or allowed to act is marked with に (or を).
points.body:
**Formation:**
- **Godan**: final u → **a + せる**: 読む → 読**ませる**, 行く → 行**かせる**, 言う → 言**わせる**
- **Ichidan**: drop る + **させる**: 食べる → 食べ**させる**
- **する** → **させる**; **来る** → **来させる (こさせる)**

**Meaning:** **make** (force) or **let** (allow), depending on context:
- 母は子供**に**野菜を食べ**させました** (made the child eat).
- 父は私**を**留学**させてくれました** (let me study abroad, kindly).

**Particle:** with transitive verbs (that have a を-object), the person takes **に**. With intransitive verbs, the person can take を or に (子供を/に行かせる).

**Asking permission:** **〜させてください** = 'please let me …': 少し休ま**せてください**, 私にやら**せてください**.
examples: {母|はは}は{子供|こども}に{野菜|やさい}を{食|た}べさせました。
The mother made her child eat vegetables.
すみません、ちょっと{休|やす}ませてください。
Excuse me, please let me rest a little.
{先生|せんせい}は{学生|がくせい}に{作文|さくぶん}を{書|か}かせました。
The teacher had the students write an essay.

points.title: させられる: be made to do (against your will)
points.summary: Causative + passive: 食べさせられる, 行かせられる / 行かされる. It expresses being forced to do something you didn't want to.
points.body:
**Formation:** take the causative form and make it passive:
- Ichidan: 食べ**させられる**
- Godan: 行か**せられる**, usually shortened to 行か**される** (u → a + **される**). The short form isn't used for verbs ending in す: 話**させられる** (not 話さされる).
- する → **させられる**; 来る → **来させられる (こさせられる)**

**Structure:** わたしは + [person who forced me]**に** + 〜させられる:
- わたしは母**に**野菜を食べ**させられました** (I was made to eat vegetables by my mother).

**Nuance:** it almost always implies the subject **didn't want to** do it. That's the difference from plain causative, which is about the person doing the forcing.
examples: {子供|こども}のとき、{母|はは}に{野菜|やさい}を{食|た}べさせられました。
As a child, I was made to eat vegetables by my mother.
{部長|ぶちょう}にお{酒|さけ}を{飲|の}まされました。
I was made to drink by the department head.
{駅|えき}で{一時間|いちじかん}も{待|ま}たされました。
I was kept waiting at the station for a whole hour.

points.title: Transitive & intransitive verb pairs
points.summary: Transitive (someone does it, with を): 開ける, 閉める, 消す, 始める. Intransitive (it happens, with が): 開く, 閉まる, 消える, 始まる.
points.body:
Many verbs come in **pairs**:
- **Transitive (他動詞)**: someone acts on something, marked with **を**: ドア**を**閉める (I close the door).
- **Intransitive (自動詞)**: something happens by itself, marked with **が**: ドア**が**閉まる (the door closes).

**Common pairs (transitive / intransitive):**
- 開ける / 開く (open)
- 閉める / 閉まる (close)
- 消す / 消える (turn off / go out)
- つける / つく (turn on)
- 始める / 始まる (begin)
- 止める / 止まる (stop)
- 落とす / 落ちる (drop / fall)
- 入れる / 入る (put in / enter)
- 出す / 出る (take out / come out)
- 壊す / 壊れる (break)

**Patterns that help:** 〜eru verbs are often transitive with an 〜aru partner (閉める/閉まる, 始める/始まる), and 〜su verbs are transitive (消す, 落とす, 出す).

**State forms:** intransitive + **ている** (窓が開いている) vs transitive + **てある** (窓が開けてある).
examples: ドアが{閉|し}まりました。
The door closed.
{部屋|へや}を{出|で}るとき、{電気|でんき}を{消|け}してください。
Please turn off the light when you leave the room.
{授業|じゅぎょう}は9{時|じ}に{始|はじ}まります。
Class starts at 9.

questions.prompt: この{漢字|かんじ}が{読|よ}（　）ますか。
questions.explanation: Godan potential: 読む → **読める** → 読めます.
notes: 読まれます is the passive ('is read').
みられ isn't a form of 読む.
まられ isn't a form.
questions.translation: Can you read this kanji?

questions.prompt: わたしは{納豆|なっとう}が{食|た}べ（　）ません。
questions.explanation: Ichidan potential: 食べる → **食べられる**.
notes: らせ isn't a form.
られさせ isn't a form.
食べさせません = 'I won't make/let (someone) eat'.
questions.translation: I can't eat natto.

questions.prompt: {来週|らいしゅう}のパーティーに（　）か。
questions.explanation: Potential of 来る: **来られる (こられる)**.
notes: The reading き is used in 来ます/来て, not in the potential.
く is only the dictionary-form reading.
こさせます is causative ('make come').
questions.translation: Can you come to next week's party?

questions.prompt: {練習|れんしゅう}して、{日本語|にほんご}で{電話|でんわ}が（　）ようになりました。
questions.explanation: The potential of する is **できる**.
notes: すれる isn't a form.
しれる isn't a form of する.
される is the passive of する.
questions.translation: With practice, I became able to make phone calls in Japanese.

questions.prompt: {姉|あね}はピアノを{弾|ひ}く（　）ができます。
questions.explanation: Ability: dictionary form + **ことができる**.
notes: ところができる isn't a pattern.
ものができる means 'a thing gets made'.
のができる isn't used for ability. It has to be こと.
questions.translation: My older sister can play the piano.

questions.prompt: この{図書館|としょかん}では、{本|ほん}を{三冊|さんさつ}まで{借|か}りる（　）できます。
questions.explanation: The fixed pattern is **ことができる**.
notes: ことをできる isn't standard. できる takes が.
のができる isn't used for ability or possibility.
ことにできる isn't the ability pattern.
questions.translation: At this library you can borrow up to three books.

questions.prompt: A：{日本語|にほんご}（　）できますか。　B：はい、{少|すこ}し。
questions.explanation: Noun + **が** + できる.
notes: できる takes が for the skill. を is a common mistake.
に doesn't mark the skill.
日本語でできますか = 'can it be done in Japanese?', a different question.
questions.translation: A: Can you speak Japanese? B: Yes, a little.

questions.prompt: {試験|しけん}がよくできたので、{先生|せんせい}に{褒|ほ}め（　）。
questions.explanation: Ichidan passive: 褒める → **褒められる**.
notes: 褒めれました is a ら-dropped form that doesn't exist for the passive.
褒めさせました = 'made someone praise'. That's causative, the wrong direction.
らせる isn't a form.
questions.translation: I did well on the test, so I was praised by my teacher.

questions.prompt: {傘|かさ}がなかったので、{雨|あめ}に{降|ふ}ら（　）、びしょびしょになりました。
questions.explanation: Suffering passive: 降る → 降**られる** (godan: る → ら + れる).
notes: 降らせて is causative ('made it rain').
降らして is colloquial causative, not passive.
られる after the あ-stem is wrong. Godan verbs take れる: 降らられる ✗.
questions.translation: I had no umbrella, so I got caught in the rain and was soaked.

questions.prompt: この{歌|うた}は{世界中|せかいじゅう}で{歌|うた}わ（　）います。
questions.explanation: Godan passive: 歌う → 歌**われる** (う → わ).
notes: Godan verbs take れる, not られる.
歌わせている = 'is making (someone) sing'.
歌わして is colloquial causative.
questions.translation: This song is sung all over the world.

questions.prompt: {楽|たの}しみにしていたのに、{弟|おとうと}にケーキを{食|た}べ（　）。
questions.explanation: Suffering passive with ichidan: 食べ**られる** ('my brother ate my cake, to my annoyance').
notes: 食べれました is a casual ら-dropped *potential* ('could eat'), not passive.
らせる isn't a form.
食べりました isn't a form.
questions.translation: I'd been looking forward to it, but my little brother ate my cake.

questions.prompt: {先生|せんせい}は{学生|がくせい}に{教科書|きょうかしょ}を{読|よ}ま（　）。
questions.explanation: Godan causative: 読む → 読**ませる**.
notes: 読まされました is causative-passive ('was made to read'), which has the wrong subject here.
さました isn't a form.
させる is for ichidan verbs. Godan verbs take せる after the あ-stem.
questions.translation: The teacher had the students read the textbook.

questions.prompt: すみません、{熱|ねつ}があるので、{今日|きょう}は{休|やす}ませて（　）。
questions.explanation: Asking permission: causative て-form + **ください** = 'please let me …'.
notes: 休ませてします isn't grammatical.
休ませていきます doesn't make sense here.
なさい needs the ます-stem and is a command.
questions.translation: Excuse me, I have a fever, so please let me take today off.

questions.prompt: {母|はは}は{子供|こども}に{部屋|へや}の{掃除|そうじ}を（　）。
questions.explanation: The causative of する is **させる**.
notes: させれる isn't a form.
すさせる isn't a form.
しさせる isn't a form.
questions.translation: The mother made her child clean the room.

questions.prompt: {子供|こども}のとき、{母|はは}に{嫌|きら}いな{野菜|やさい}を{食|た}べ（　）。
questions.explanation: Ichidan causative-passive: 食べ**させられる** (causative first, then passive).
notes: させりました isn't a form.
されさせました isn't a form.
The order is wrong: causative (させ) comes before passive (られ).
questions.translation: As a child, I was made to eat vegetables I hated by my mother.

questions.prompt: {飲|の}み{会|かい}で、{部長|ぶちょう}にお{酒|さけ}をたくさん{飲|の}ま（　）。
questions.explanation: Godan short causative-passive: 飲む → 飲ま**される** (= 飲ませられる).
notes: させれる isn't a form.
さられる isn't a form.
せれる isn't a form. The long form is 飲ませられる.
questions.translation: At the drinking party, I was made to drink a lot by the department head.

questions.prompt: What does 「{駅|えき}で{一時間|いちじかん}も{待|ま}たされました」 mean?
options: I made someone wait at the station for an hour.
I was kept waiting at the station for an hour.
Someone waited for me for an hour.
I could wait for an hour.
questions.explanation: 待た**される** = causative-passive: 'was made to wait'.
notes: 'Made someone wait' is the plain causative: 待たせました.
'Someone waited for me' would be 待ってくれました / 待ってもらいました.
'Could wait' is the potential: 待てました.

questions.prompt: {風|かぜ}でドアが（　）。
questions.explanation: With **が** and no person acting: intransitive **閉まる**.
notes: 閉める is transitive and needs を and someone doing it (ドアを閉めました).
閉まめる isn't a verb.
閉める isn't 閉めり-. That isn't a form.
questions.translation: The door closed because of the wind.

questions.prompt: {部屋|へや}を{出|で}るとき、{電気|でんき}を（　）ください。
questions.explanation: 電気**を**: transitive **消す** → 消して.
notes: きえて (消える) is intransitive ('go out') and can't take を.
けえて isn't a form of either verb.
きして isn't a form.
questions.translation: Please turn off the light when you leave the room.

questions.prompt: {授業|じゅぎょう}は9{時|じ}に（　）。
questions.explanation: Class (は/が) starts by itself: intransitive **始まる**.
notes: 始めまります isn't a form.
始める is transitive (先生が授業を始めます). With 授業 as the subject, use 始まる.
始まえる isn't a verb.
questions.translation: Class starts at 9.

questions.prompt: あっ、{財布|さいふ}を（　）しまいました。
questions.explanation: 財布**を**: transitive **落とす** ('drop') → 落として.
notes: 落とちて isn't a form.
落ちる is intransitive ('fall') and can't take を.
落ちとして isn't a form.
questions.translation: Oh no, I dropped my wallet.
